title: Perfect Rice
description:
There are all kinds of ways to make rice, but this is the recipe that we’ve always used. It came from a little article in The New York Times – “A Perfect Batch of Rice” – way back when we were first living there.
This rice always comes out just right – perfect – and it’s super easy, basically 1 part rice to 1 ½ parts liquid. There is also a big added benefit that you know precisely when it’ll be done – 17 minutes after you put it in the oven – so you don’t have to worry about it while working on other dishes. And, if you’re a little behind schedule with other things, it’ll stay nice and warm in the hot dish.
Of course, you can always “kick it up a notch,” as Emeril would say, with extra spices added to the broth, or sautéing some onions and or garlic or diced vegetables in the butter for a moment before cooking the rice.
Perfect Rice
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees.
Heat 2 tablespoons butter in an ovenproof saucepan or bowl that has a lid.
If you’re sautéing some onions or other additions, cook them in the butter for a couple of minutes until they wilt a bit.
ingredients: Add the rice and stir until the grains are coated.
directions: Add salt to taste, maybe some pepper or a pinch of cayenne pepper or a dash or two of Tabasco sauce. You could add a sprig of fresh thyme or a sprinkling of dried thyme.
Add the chicken broth and bay leaf and bring the broth and rice mixture to a boil.
At the boil, give the mixture a stir, cover the dish, and place it in the oven.
Bake the rice for precisely 17 minutes.
Remove from the oven and serve!
